headline: Turn-level action selection improves reported agent success with substantial token overhead
summary: A 4 November arXiv preprint evaluates turn-level best-of-N (Turn-BoN): at each step, a generator proposes 4 or 8 candidate tool actions and a separate language-model selector chooses one before it is executed. On 89 Terminal-Bench v2.1 tasks across four trials, the authors report higher pass rates for Qwen3.6-35B and K2-Horizon-375B generators when paired with Kimi-K3 or DeepSeek V4.1 Flash selectors. Reported gains include K2-Horizon 73.3% to 77.9% at N=4 and Qwen3.6 47.5% to 52.8% at N=4 or 55.2% at N=8. The authors also report 40–50% fewer turns and reduced looping, while output tokens rise to about 3.6–8.2 times baseline. These preliminary paper-reported results use two generator models and stronger selectors; they were not independently reproduced.
